description: Code, frozen protocol, derived data and full results for a benchmark of probabilistic load forecasting in extreme cold in PJM and MISO: 13 modelled events from 2014 to 2026 (PJM: January 2014 polar vortex, 2017-18 cold snap, January 2019 polar vortex, December 2022 Winter Storm Elliott, January 2024, 2025 and 2026 cold; MISO: 2017-18, 2019, 2022, 2024, 2025, 2026), plus a February 2015 operator-error anchor. Three forecasters and eight recalibration methods are evaluated under strictly chronological evaluation and under retrospective leave-one-event-out transfer. Findings: uncalibrated 90% interval coverage is lower inside the event than over the full evaluation period in all 13 events (sign test over seven distinct weather events, p = 0.008); no calibrator meets the repair conditions in any event; retrospective and chronological coverage differ by up to 50 points with a sign that varies between systems; refitting the benchmark on archived day-ahead GEFS forecasts keeps the collapse in 9 of 13 events and the repair failure in all 13. Version 1.2.0 adds amendments A5 (ensemble-spread calibrator C5), A6 (seven further events), A7 (temperature-weighted conformal C6 and conditional generalised Pareto tails C7) and A8 (forecast weather throughout), whose plans were published in this repository before their data were downloaded or their analyses run, together with all figures and their scripts.
title: PJM and MISO Cold-Spell Calibration Benchmark: When Cold-Spell Calibration Fails to Transfer
